`interface IResourceDecoder`<br/>
**Known subtypes:** [`AnimatedResourceDecoder`](/reference/resources/animatedresourcedecoder/), [`RasterResourceDecoder`](/reference/resources/rasterresourcedecoder/), [`VectorResourceDecoder`](/reference/resources/vectorresourcedecoder/), [`VideoResourceDecoder`](/reference/resources/videoresourcedecoder/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.resource.decoder` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [IResourceDecoder.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/resource/decoder/IResourceDecoder.java)

Reads the data of one resource, decodes it on a background thread and sends it to the GPU on the render thread.

## Description

An [`IResourceFormat`](/reference/resources/iresourceformat/) creates one per resource.
JOID calls `prepare` on the thread that first draws the resource, `decode` on a loading thread (or on the drawing thread for a blocking resource), then `upload` on the render thread; `clear` frees what the decoder holds.
Fill the [`ResourceData`](/reference/resources/resourcedata/) you are given: its size, its pixels or its textures.

- [Custom formats](/use/learn/going-further/custom-formats/)

## Method details

<a id="IResourceDecoder-method-prepare"></a>

### prepare

`void prepare(ResourceData resource)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

JOID calls it before each decode, on the thread that draws: create the textures there, for example with [`ResourceData.placeholder`](/reference/resources/resourcedata/#ResourceData-method-placeholder).
An exception makes the resource fail.

<a id="IResourceDecoder-method-decode"></a>

### decode

`void decode(ResourceData resource)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

JOID calls it on a loading thread: read the asset and set the size and the pixels of `resource`.
An exception makes the resource fail, unless a reload replaced this decode.

<a id="IResourceDecoder-method-upload"></a>

### upload

`void upload(ResourceData resource)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

JOID calls it on the render thread once the pixels are decoded: send them to the textures, for example with [`ResourceData.uploadTextures`](/reference/resources/resourcedata/#ResourceData-method-uploadTextures).

<a id="IResourceDecoder-method-clear"></a>

### clear

`void clear(ResourceData resource)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

JOID calls it when the resource is cleared or reloaded: free what the decoder holds, such as a file or a native handle.

<a id="IResourceDecoder-method-fork"></a>

### fork

`IResourceDecoder fork()` <span class="joid-qualifier">default</span>

Returns a decoder for a separate playback of the same file, or `null` when the resource has no playback to separate; `null` by default.

<a id="IResourceDecoder-method-isSettled"></a>

### isSettled

`boolean isSettled()` <span class="joid-qualifier">default</span>

If `true`, the decoder has nothing left to update, so that a frame that draws it can be compared with a reference; `true` by default.

<a id="IResourceDecoder-method-isMipmappable"></a>

### isMipmappable

`boolean isMipmappable()` <span class="joid-qualifier">default</span>

If `true`, the textures accept mipmaps; `true` by default.

<a id="IResourceDecoder-method-init"></a>

### init

`void init(ResourceData resource)` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">default</span>

JOID calls it when the decoder is attached to `resource`; empty by default.

<a id="IResourceDecoder-method-update"></a>

### update

`void update(ResourceData resource)` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">default</span>

JOID calls it each time the resource is bound for drawing, on the render thread: advance an animation there; empty by default.

<a id="IResourceDecoder-method-request"></a>

### request

`void request(ResourceData resource, int width, int height, boolean async, boolean resizing)` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">default</span>

JOID calls it on each draw with the size the resource covers in screen pixels; `async` tells whether to work in the background and `resizing` that the size changed less than 200 ms ago.
A vector decoder renders again at that size; empty by default.
